finding: The delta tells step 7 to put an existing plan/DECISIONS.md entry id into the record, but the Record table has no field that holds a decision id and no step sets one. A new two-way-door entry's id is never put into the record, so only the reused case reaches it, and no caller reads that id.
why: The Record section is the procedure's output contract: skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:203 "The caller keeps the record in its own report." and its table (IN-PLACE-FIX.md:205-216) lists every field with the step that sets it. A field set by step 7 but missing from that table is a drifted twin of the contract.
fix: Either add a Record row such as "| Decisions | steps 3, 7 | each `plan/DECISIONS.md` entry id the fix recorded or reused |" and write the id there in both cases, or drop "put its id into the record" and say only "record no new entry".
evidence: skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:179-181 "A two-way door is recorded, and the SDD goes into the record as stale; when `plan/DECISIONS.md` already holds an entry for that decision, put its id into the record instead of a new entry." vs IN-PLACE-FIX.md:205-216, whose rows are Failure, Runs, Code caller/Input/Failing path, Edits, Tiers, Miss class, Stale artifacts, Lesson, Rationale and Reason; none holds a decision id. Method: read the Record table whole and grepped skills/afk/fix/ for "DECISIONS"; the only consumer-side hit, skills/afk/fix/SKILL.md:37, records a decision in Phase 1 and reads no id back from the record.

finding: The delta changed the lesson half of this sentence to depend on what the record holds, but left the miss-class half depending on whether Phase 2.5 ran. Phase 2.5 runs procedure step 6, which skips a pure unit or logic bug and names no miss class. So 'Phase 2.5 ran' can hold when there is no class to add, and an agent must either make one up or ignore the rule.
why: Delta-sweep item (skills/afk/review/checklists/delta-sweep.md:8): "a fix applied at one site while a sibling path keeps the old behaviour". skills/afk/fix/ESCAPE-ANALYSIS.md:9-11 "Run only for **standing-suite tier** bugs ... Skip a pure unit/logic bug that never had a higher-tier scenario"; IN-PLACE-FIX.md:212 "| Miss class | steps 1, 6 | the escape-analysis class, when one was named |".
fix: Make both halves depend on the record: "the record holds a miss class → add the **miss class** to the summary; procedure step 8 recorded a lesson → append the **lesson id** ...".
evidence: skills/afk/fix/SKILL.md:81 "Phase 2.5 ran → add the **miss class** to the summary; procedure step 8 recorded a lesson → append the **lesson id** so the workflow-improvement lesson isn't lost:"; SKILL.md:53 "Run [IN-PLACE-FIX.md](IN-PLACE-FIX.md) step 6. A `blocked` return → report `blocked`, naming it. Carry the miss class into Phase 4's report."

finding: Possible missing branch. The delta made the Live tiers exit restore a reverted fix, but that exit fires only when no instance or no restart command was handed over. Nothing covers a restart command that was handed over but fails, for example when the instance will not start on the reverted tree in step 4 or step 6. The check then can never run, because it runs 'only after' a restart that never happened, and no exit, result or restore is stated.
why: The brief treats an instruction an agent cannot carry out, or a missing branch, as a defect. IN-PLACE-FIX.md:43-45 makes a live check conditional on a completed restart, and IN-PLACE-FIX.md:220-222 says `blocked` keeps the edits made so far, which holds only when the fix is restored before the return.
fix: Widen the exit's condition to every case where a live check cannot run: "A live check with no instance or no restart command handed over, or whose restart fails → restore the step 3 fix when a step reverted it, then return `blocked`, naming the check and the restart's output."
evidence: skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:43-47 "A check that runs against the running instance runs, in any step, only after the caller's restart command has restarted that instance on the current working tree. A live check with no instance or no restart command handed over → restore the step 3 fix when a step reverted it, then return `blocked`, naming the check."; IN-PLACE-FIX.md:115-118 "Watch each test this step adds fail with the step 3 fix reverted ... A live-tier test follows \"Live tiers\" for each of the two runs." Method: grepped skills/afk/fix/ for "restart"; hits are IN-PLACE-FIX.md:18, :44-45 and SKILL.md:14, :28, and none names a failed restart.

finding: Phase 0 step 5 decides at intake, before diagnosis, whether to ask for the running instance and restart command. It asks only when the reported bug is one a live tier must prove. Phase 2 can still add a live test later, through procedure step 4's Contract row (api) or its user-visible-flow row (e2e/browser), once the diagnosis shows the bug's class. Example: a ticket reporting a wrong total is diagnosed as a status-code bug, so step 4 adds an api test. No instance was asked for at intake, so the Live tiers rule ends the run `blocked`, and the skill has no instruction to ask then, though a human is present to answer.
why: SKILL.md:14 "Its running instance and restart command are the ones Phase 0 step 5 takes; with none, a live tier ends the procedure `blocked`." The only re-ask covers a worktree change (SKILL.md:28 "Ask again when Phase 1 step 3 puts the fix in a worktree the named command does not serve."), not a live tier first needed after diagnosis.
fix: In Phase 0 step 5 (or Phase 2), ask for the instance and restart command whenever procedure step 4 or 5 is about to run a live check and the invoker named none. End `blocked` only when the invoker cannot supply them.
evidence: SKILL.md:28 "A bug a live tier must prove (`api`, `e2e/browser`, or a check in the running UI) needs the running instance and a command that restarts it on the fix's working tree. Take both from the invoker and ask for each one the invoker did not name."; IN-PLACE-FIX.md:126 "| Contract / envelope / authz / status-code | Yes — it's a backend contract | `api` ..."; IN-PLACE-FIX.md:45-47 "A live check with no instance or no restart command handed over → restore the step 3 fix when a step reverted it, then return `blocked`"

finding: Fixed key f009 makes the procedure run `rationale-drop` on every pending entry when a revert removes the fix's uncommitted edits. RATIONALE.md, the one home for the drop verb, still says to use it for an entry whose line a later commit rewrote or deleted, and names no revert of uncommitted edits.
why: AGENTS.md 'DRY - one fact, one home': the owning file states when a verb applies, and a pointer that widens the use leaves the owner stale. RATIONALE.md:62-63 is the passage the f009 finding quoted as too narrow, and it did not change. Pattern used: grep of the identifier `rationale-drop` in RATIONALE.md and IN-PLACE-FIX.md, then read both in context.
fix: Widen RATIONALE.md:62-63 to 'Use it for an entry whose line a later commit rewrote or deleted, or whose uncommitted line a revert removed', and record the edit outside the 0006 Scope in the decision ledger.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:218-221 "`design_conflict`, `needs_decision` and `flaky` leave no edit of the fix in the working tree, tests included: before returning, revert each edit and run `rationale-drop` (`RATIONALE.md` § Write path) on each pending operation the fix recorded." vs RATIONALE.md:62-63 "6. Withdraw: `… rationale-drop --op <id> --reason <text>`. Use it for an entry whose line a later commit rewrote or deleted."
